content: Terbutaline is a medication prescribed to manage and alleviate symptoms such as wheezing, shortness of breath, and difficulty breathing caused by conditions like asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, and other lung diseases. It works by relaxing and opening the airways in the lungs, making it easier to breathe. While it is primarily used for these purposes, it may also be prescribed for other conditions. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Terbutaline is available in two forms: oral tablets and an inhaler. The tablets are typically taken three times a day, while the inhaler is used as needed to relieve symptoms or every 4-6 hours to prevent them. It is essential to follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use terbutaline exactly as directed, without altering the dose or frequency unless instructed by your doctor. This medication helps control symptoms but does not cure the underlying condition. Continue using it even if you feel well, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. If you are using the terbutaline inhaler for the first time, read the accompanying instructions carefully. Ask your doctor, pharmacist, or respiratory therapist to demonstrate the correct technique, and practice using the inhaler under their supervision. To use the inhaler properly: 1. Shake the inhaler thoroughly. 2. Remove the protective cap. 3. Exhale completely through your nose while keeping your mouth closed. 4. For the open-mouth technique, hold the inhaler 1-2 inches away from your open mouth. For the closed-mouth technique, place the mouthpiece well into your mouth, past your front teeth, and seal your lips tightly around it. 5. Take a slow, deep breath through the mouthpiece while pressing down on the container to release the medication. 6. Hold your breath for 5-10 seconds, then remove the inhaler and exhale slowly through your nose or mouth. 7. If a second puff is required, wait 2 minutes, shake the inhaler again, and repeat the process. 8. Replace the protective cap after use. If you have difficulty using the inhaler effectively, a spacer device may help. Consult your doctor, pharmacist, or respiratory therapist for guidance. In addition to its primary uses, terbutaline tablets are sometimes prescribed to prevent premature labor during pregnancy. In such cases, the tablets are usually taken every 4-6 hours until delivery. Discuss the potential risks and benefits of this treatment with your doctor. Before using terbutaline, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to terbutaline or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, and supplements you are taking, especially atenolol, carteolol, labetalol, metoprolol, nadolol, propranolol, sotalol, timolol, phenelzine, tranylcypromine, theophylline, or medications containing ephedrine, phenylephrine, phenylpropanolamine, or pseudoephedrine. Many over-the-counter products, such as diet pills and cold medications, may contain these substances, so check labels carefully and consult your doctor before use. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, notify your doctor. If you become pregnant while using terbutaline, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are using terbutaline. If you miss a dose of terbutaline, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Terbutaline may cause mild side effects, including tremors, nervousness, dizziness, drowsiness, weakness, headache, upset stomach, flushing, sweating, dry mouth, or throat irritation. If these symptoms persist or worsen, inform your doctor. Severe side effects, such as increased difficulty breathing, rapid or irregular heartbeat, or chest pain, require immediate medical attention. Report any serious side effects to your doctor or the FDA’s MedWatch program. Store terbutaline in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for disposal instructions. Avoid puncturing the container, and do not discard it in a fire or incinerator. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or stops breathing, call emergency services at 911. Attend all scheduled appointments with your doctor and laboratory, as they may order tests to monitor your response to terbutaline. To alleviate dry mouth or throat irritation caused by the inhaler, rinse your mouth with water, chew gum, or suck on sugarless hard candy after use. Clean the inhaler weekly by removing the drug container, washing the mouthpiece with warm water, and drying it thoroughly. Do not share your medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription. Terbutaline is sold under the brand name Brethine®.
